event_note: Keysight's 2026-11-02 CFO-succession release says results for the quarter ended 2026-10-31 come on Thursday 19 Nov as scheduled (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/KEYS/2611023301). Zacks says after the closing bell (https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3030409/can-strong-revenue-growth-boost-keysights-q4-earnings, snippet only). The last two calls were at 1:30 pm PT after the close, and the front 2026-11-20 expiry carries 155% ATM IV, so the print is amc. No 2026 date-and-time release was retrieved; Chartmill's 23 Nov date is contradicted by the company.
conviction_note: Direct counterparties that reported after Keysight last spoke all point to data-center test demand holding through October: Viavi's core data-center business ex-Spirent more than doubled, Coherent guided FY27 above 60% and NVDA guided Q4 to $130bn. Keysight itself said on 2 Nov, after the quarter closed, that demand 'remains strong' and left the guide alone. The stock is down 14% in a month on an AI and rates de-rating, with upside skew paid. Against that, this name sold its last two beats (-0.6%, -6.3%), management has said supply will govern revenue conversion for several quarters, and the Q1 FY27 bar the stock will trade on cannot be sourced. That is a small lean of p_up 55 on an abs_move of 9.5, giving +0.95. impact_sum (+2.4) is larger because it adds several small same-direction proxies, each sized on its own. The supply-capped Q1 guide is the one finding that could flip the sign.
bar: Q4 FY26 company guide: revenue $1.930-1.950bn, non-GAAP EPS $3.34-3.40 (Q3 release, https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20623224, 2026-08-18; reaffirmed 'not updating' 2026-11-02, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/KEYS/2611023301). Consensus: Earnings Whispers $3.36 / $1.94bn, whisper $3.49 (https://finviz.com/news/421346/keysights-supply-chain-not-demand-sets-the-bar-for-a-record-fourth-quarter, 2026-11-11); Chartmill $3.44 / $1.985bn (snippet only). The two estimate sources disagree, so the reported-quarter bar is anchored on the company guide, and the real bar sits above it (the whisper is above the top of the range). The Q1 FY27 guide bar, the line most likely to move the stock, is UNSOURCED: no Q1 consensus was found. The guidance findings are capped small for that reason.
positioning_check: Short interest: about 2.9M shares, about 1.7% of float, 3.1 days to cover at the 2026-08-14 settlement, per a FINRA-based tracker (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/keys/short-interest/, snippet; no November reading found). Not a crowded short. Skew: 25-delta put minus call is -2.51 vol points, so upside is paid. Put/call OI is 0.78. Straddle-implied move is 9.18% against a 6.32% median historical reaction. Tape: -6.34% over 5 days, -8.53% over 20 days, -26.6% off the 52-week high, and -12.4% since the August print against an S&P 500 down 1.4%. The bullish-sentiment reading has dropped to 28.3% from 35.8% before the last report (finviz/EW 2026-11-11). Macro inside the window: an AI-trade unwind (SOX about -9% on 2026-11-05), the 10-year at 5.12%, and Nvidia's CEO resigning on 2026-11-12.

findings.finding: Viavi (VIAV), Keysight's closest listed rival in network and data-center test, reported on 2026-11-04 for the quarter ended 2026-10-03, which overlaps Keysight's Aug-Oct quarter. NSE revenue was +74.1% YoY to $376.1M, and the CEO said the core data-center test business ex-Spirent more than doubled YoY, with production test growing fastest. Q2 FY27 is guided to $505-515M, about +9% sequential against $469.3M. Keysight's own Q4 guide is +5% sequential.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: KEYS's forward-guide prints have paid: Q4 FY25 (+10.0%) and Q1 FY26 (+23.1%), both on guides well above consensus. Q3 FY26 also guided far above (Q4 EPS guide $3.34-3.40 against $2.72 consensus) and fell 6.3%, on a day test names were sold sector-wide.
findings.why_not_priced: The read-through is public. Since it landed, KEYS has fallen with the AI complex rather than re-rated on it (the stock was $305 on 11-11 and is $285 now). If the market were carrying Viavi's data-center doubling into KEYS's Q1 guide, the stock would not be at the bottom of its post-earnings range with sentiment at 28% bullish.
findings.independence: Viavi's own release (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/VIAV/2611048509, 2026-11-04) has the revenue and guide numbers. The data-center-core-doubling remark is from Zacks/barchart call coverage. This is a peer and competitor, not a customer, so it is a proxy for Keysight's wireline orders.

findings.finding: Coherent (COHR), an optical-transceiver maker that buys high-speed optical and electrical test, reported FQ1 2027 revenue of $2.37bn against a $2.30bn estimate in early November 2026. It guided FY27 pro-forma revenue growth above 60% and said it sees no attenuation in customer demand, with output capacity as the constraint. Lumentum said in August that 1.6T uptake intensifies through calendar 2027. This is the 1.6T optical ramp Keysight names as its wireline growth driver.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Wireline/AI-driven orders were what lifted KEYS's guides in Nov 2025 and Feb 2026 (+10.0%, +23.1%). Wireline has now overtaken wireless in revenue (finviz/EW preview 2026-11-11).
findings.source_date: 2026-11 (early November; exact day not on page)
findings.why_not_priced: Coherent's growth guide reached the market during the same week as the SOX -9% day. KEYS, a second-derivative beneficiary, has fallen 14% in a month since. A priced read-through would show KEYS holding up against the AI complex, and it has not.
findings.independence: This is a different document from the Viavi finding: a customer-side series, not a competitor. Lumentum's August guide (https://finviz.com/news/380953/lumentum-beats-quarterly-forecasts-as-ai-demand-drives-stronger-outlook) points the same way. Both are proxies; Keysight has not confirmed Coherent as a named customer.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-02, two days after the Q4 quarter closed on 10-31, Keysight said in the CFO-succession release that it is 'not updating' its Q4 outlook ($1.93-1.95bn, $3.34-3.40) and that 'demand across its end markets remains strong and it continues to execute well'. This is a post-quarter-close statement, which rules out a warning-sized miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior instance of an intra-quarter reaffirmation by KEYS in the baseline. On the reported quarter, Q2 FY26 beat the top of guide by about 1% and the stock fell 0.6%; Q3 FY26 beat the revenue midpoint by about 6% and fell 6.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: it was public on 11-02 and the stock then fell with the sector. What it adds is that the company had closed books in hand when it chose not to warn. Lands inside guidance, so sized near 0.
findings.independence: This is the same document the sweep used for event confirmation. Nothing else points the same way.

findings.finding: Keysight's last three quarters beat its own revenue guide midpoint by +3.9% (Q1 FY26: $1.60bn against $1.53-1.55bn), +1.2% (Q2: $1.72bn against $1.69-1.71bn) and +6.1% (Q3: $1.846bn against $1.73-1.75bn). Q4 is guided only +5% sequential because of supply. A typical beat therefore puts Q4 at about $1.97-2.00bn against the $1.94bn guide midpoint and EW consensus, but at or below Chartmill's $1.985bn and around the EPS whisper of $3.49.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reported-quarter beats on their own have not been bought: Q2 FY26 -0.6%, Q3 FY26 -6.3% on a 25% EPS beat. The positive reactions (+10.0%, +23.1%) came with new-period guides.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the whisper of $3.49 sits above the guided range, so a beat is expected. The residual is that supply-limited quarters (the Q3 guide was also supply-aware) still beat by 6%.
findings.independence: The Q2 release (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/2024454/keysight-technologies-reports-second-quarter-2026-results) and the Q1 release (https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20409724) give the earlier guide and actual pairs. These are company documents, but they are history, not this quarter.

findings.finding: Management said on the Q3 call (2026-08-18) that supply is 'likely to be nonlinear and will likely be a governor of our ability to convert demand into revenue' for several quarters. The constraint has moved to incoming parts that competitors also source, and the supply environment is 'less flexible today than a year ago'. Inventory was flat at $1.047bn against $1.050bn at FY-end (Q3 10-Q). Q1 has historically been flat-ish to Q4 (Q4 FY24 $1.29bn to Q1 FY25 $1.30bn). The Q1 FY27 guide could therefore land at or below a street that models growth. Teradyne guided Q4 flat sequential on 10-27, fell about 6% after hours and 21% over the following week.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: KEYS has not issued a disappointing new-period guide in the 7-print baseline. The peer pattern (Teradyne: beat, flat guide, sold) is the template for this risk.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the EW preview frames supply as the bar. But no Q1 consensus was found, so it is unknowable whether the street's Q1 already embeds a supply-capped flat sequential. If it did, the skew would not be paying upside.
findings.independence: Teradyne Q4 guide (https://247wallst.com/cards/teradyne-q3-2026-earnings-ter-01m60ztabhwe15pys2j1erv5ns, 2026-10-27) is a peer, production-semi test rather than R&D test, so the link is loose. Inventory comes from the Q3 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001601046/000160104626000036/keys-20260731.htm). Short interest is about 1.7% of float, so there is no squeeze against this negative.

findings.finding: FY26 profitability carries a one-time IEEPA tariff recovery: a $100M receivable booked in FY26, with $93M offset to cost of sales, plus a $40M customer-refund liability against revenue. Management said this 'artificially pulled up 26 profitability' and won't repeat, so any FY27 margin framing given tonight starts from a lower adjusted base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no KEYS reaction on a tariff item. In the resolved record, tariff refunds were noise next to the direction of guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: management flagged it and the EW preview repeats it. The residual is whether Q1 FY27 EPS guidance looks like a sequential step-down once it is stripped out.
findings.independence: The same call transcript as the supply finding carries the 'won't repeat' quote. The 10-Q is a separate primary document for the dollars.

findings.finding: The bar has been reset lower by the tape, not by the company. KEYS is -12.4% since the August print against an S&P 500 down 1.4%, -14% over the month and -26.6% off its high. Bullish sentiment is down to 28.3% from 35.8%. The 25-delta skew is -2.5 (upside paid) and short interest is low. The fall tracks the AI-trade unwind (SOX about -9% on 11-05), the 10-year at 5.12% and Nvidia's CEO resigning on 11-12, not anything Keysight-specific. Nvidia's Q3 on 11-17 ($115.8bn, +103% YoY, Q4 guide $130bn) left the underlying AI-infrastructure demand intact.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 reaction (-6.3%) coincided with a sector-wide test-equipment profit-taking day with no company catalyst (247wallst 2026-08-19). That shows this name's post-print move is partly the sector tape, which cuts both ways.
findings.why_not_priced: The de-rating is the price. The question is whether it holds a company-specific worry, and nothing Keysight-specific was found: no downgrade, no warning, and the company said demand is strong. If the drop were about Keysight, the skew would be put-bid, not call-bid.
findings.independence: Macro context comes from https://www.wealthprofessional.ca/investments/equity-markets/wall-street-absorbs-the-hit-as-nvidia-touches-a-52-week-low/394013 (2026-11-13) and https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/11/06/tech-stock-rout-accelerates-retreat-from-the-ai-trade (2026-11-06). The skew is from the sealed baseline. The same macro tape could keep pressing the stock after the print.

findings.finding: Nvidia reported fiscal Q3 2027 revenue of $115.8bn (+103% YoY, +20% QoQ) on 2026-11-17 and guided Q4 to $130bn ±3%. That is the AI-compute build Keysight's data-center and semiconductor customers design into.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and two days old, so mostly priced. KEYS still fell into it (5-day -6.3%), so the market is not reading NVDA's guide through to test demand.
findings.independence: This is macro-to-company transmission: Keysight has not confirmed it. It is a different document from the Viavi and Coherent findings.

findings.finding: Applied Materials reported fiscal Q4 2026 revenue of $10.41bn (+53%) on 2026-11-12 and guided Q1 FY27 to $11.1bn ±$0.5bn, against $10.89bn consensus. Semiconductor capex, which feeds Keysight's semiconductor and EISG customers, is holding into calendar 2027.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and mostly priced. Semi-equipment strength has not stopped test names falling with the AI complex.
findings.independence: This is an industry proxy and loosely linked. AMAT's own release is at https://ir.appliedmaterials.com/news-releases/news-release-details/applied-materials-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2026.

findings.finding: Emerson's Test & Measurement segment (NI, Keysight's general-purpose electronic-test competitor) grew sales 14% to $465M, 15% underlying, in the September 2026 quarter, against +12% a year earlier. General electronics test demand outside AI is firm, which bears on EISG (27% of Keysight revenue, +21% in Q3).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a small segment of a large industrial and nobody models KEYS off it. The effect is small either way.
findings.independence: This is a peer proxy. The 14% figure is from Zacks coverage rather than read off the release.

findings.finding: Capital return: Keysight authorized a $1.5bn buyback with its Q4 FY25 report in Nov 2025 and repurchased $520M over nine months of FY26 ($211M in Q3). Cash and restricted cash stood at $2.62bn with Q3 free cash flow of $403M. That leaves room for a new or enlarged authorization at the Q4 report, the same slot as last year's.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Nov 2025 authorization came with a +10.0% reaction, mostly attributable to the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inference: there is no signal of a new authorization. Small.
findings.independence: The Q3 10-Q gives the repurchase pace (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001601046/000160104626000036/keys-20260731.htm).

findings.finding: The CFO changes on 2026-12-18: Neil Dougherty (13 years as CFO) hands over to Jason Kary, who was Treasurer and Head of IR from 2014 to 2024 and has run EISG since. Dougherty stays as an adviser through FY27, and tonight is his last print as CFO. An orderly, internal, IR-literate successor makes a 'kitchen-sink' guide less likely.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced; the announcement came with a reaffirmation.
findings.independence: This is the same document as the 11-02 reaffirmation finding.

outside_window.finding: The CFO transition takes effect on 2026-12-18, after the exit window.

baseline_tension: The findings agree with the skew (upside paid) and cut against the run-up (-8.5% over 20 days, -6.3% over 5 days). The run-up is explained by sector and macro, not by anything company-specific, so the lean is long but small. The sold-beats history and the unsourced Q1 bar hold p_up at 55.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): cut the reported-quarter beat-history finding from +0.5 to +0.3, because the last two beats were sold (-0.6%, -6.3%).
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): cut the 11-02 post-close reaffirmation from +0.3 to +0.2, because it lands inside guidance the market was told to expect.
Lesson 6 (bar unsourced): capped the supply-capped Q1 guide negative from -1.5 to -1.0, because the Q1 FY27 consensus it depends on could not be sourced.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): cut the IEEPA tariff non-repeat from -0.3 to -0.2. It is a below-gross-margin one-off already flagged by management, sized only on its path into FY27 margin framing.

Lesson 7: short interest was looked up (about 1.7% of float, 3.1 days) before the negative was filed; it is not crowded, so the negative was not shrunk on that ground. The positive sign agrees with the skew.
Lessons 5 and 9: the peer and macro proxies (Viavi, Coherent, NVDA, AMAT, Emerson) stay filed small, with independence saying so; the scaled measurement did not move.
